procedure_evidence: Activation instructions cover inspection, screening, auditing, and metadata listing of untrusted TAR/ZIP archives, while excluding creation, trusted extraction, general compression questions, and member-payload access.
Invocation resolves the helper relative to SKILL.md and requires caller-supplied positive entry-count and declared-size budgets.
Instructions define stable safe/unsafe/error statuses with exit codes 0/1/2 and a single JSON result.
The workflow prohibits automatic extraction and reserves the extraction decision and action for a human.
The claim boundary explicitly says safe is only a metadata-policy result, not evidence of authenticity, malware freedom, payload safety, or extraction safety.
privacy_evidence: The helper uses tarfile and zipfile metadata APIs without extraction, member-payload opening, network access, subprocesses, or archive mutation.
Name validation rejects empty names, POSIX absolute paths, Windows drives, UNC paths after separator normalization, slash/backslash parent components, and ASCII controls.
The code rejects TAR symbolic/hard links and special types, ZIP Unix symlinks and special types, and encrypted ZIP entries.
It detects normalized duplicates and case-folded collisions and checks entry-count and cumulative declared-size budgets without accessing member payloads.

It emits one compact JSON object with ordered issue codes; handles invalid arguments, missing inputs, malformed archives, and supported archive exceptions; uses Python-3.9-compatible constructs; and reports only a bounded metadata-policy verdict.
limitations: Assessment is source-only as required: the candidate helper was not executed, so no deterministic runtime results are inferred.
